lines.say: Fifteen million dollars. Enron's former CEO netted more than that from one stock sale, on September seventeenth, two thousand one, the day markets reopened after nine eleven.
lines.show: $15 million. Enron's former CEO netted more than that from one stock sale, on September 17, 2001, the day markets reopened after 9/11.

scene.label: from one sale
scene.src: Brief for the United States, No. 08-1394

lines.say: He told his broker he didn't want people at Enron to know. Under oath, he said he sold because he was scared by September eleventh.
lines.show: He told his broker he didn't want people at Enron to know. Under oath, he said he sold because he was "scared" by September 11.

scene.src: Brief for the United States, No. 08-1394

lines.say: Less than three months later, Enron was bankrupt. The jury acquitted him on nine insider-trading counts. This sale was the one it convicted him on.
Real trials. Real evidence. The verdict.
